summary: Removed the `intro`, `details`, and `verify` intermediate steps, cutting the funnel from 6 steps to 3, because each additional step in a signup funnel causes ~20–50% drop-off, and the eliminated steps (company philosophy, details, email re-verification) add friction without gating any real value.

Replaced the generic welcome page with a benefit-driven headline, three concrete objection-busting bullets ("free," "no hidden fees," "instant start"), and a prominent styled CTA that reads "무료로 시작하기 →" instead of the vague "자세히 알아보기" — removing the ambiguity of what clicking does and reducing perceived risk, which directly lifts click-through to the email step.

Replaced the separate-page CTA link with an inline email form that submits directly to `/confirm`, eliminating the intermediate `/step1` page and reducing the funnel from 3 steps to 2 — fewer clicks to completion is one of the highest-impact changes for improving signup conversion.

Added a social proof block (user count + testimonial) directly above the sign-up form, because showing that 12,400 real people already use the product reduces hesitation and activates herd behavior, which is one of the most reliable drivers of signup conversion.

Added a fixed urgency announcement bar at the top of the page offering 60 days of premium features free "this week only," which gives hesitant visitors a concrete, time-limited reason to sign up now rather than returning later.

Added a second testimonial from a startup founder (complementing the freelancer persona) and a star rating (★★★★★ 4.9/5) next to the user count, providing broader social proof that appeals to multiple audience segments and reinforces trust at the critical moment of signup decision.
